title: Small Fry Club
text: Small Fry Club is a children's television program that was broadcast on the DuMont Television Network. It debuted on March 11, 1947, with the title Movies for Small Fry and ended on June 15, 1951.

title: Juvenile Jury
text: Juvenile Jury is an American children's game show that originally ran on NBC from April 3, 1947, to August 1, 1954. It was hosted by Jack Barry and featured a panel of children aged ten or less giving advice to solve the problems of other children.

title: Kraft Television Theatre
text: Kraft Television Theatre is an American anthology drama television series running from 1947 to 1958. It began May 7, 1947, on NBC, airing at 7:30 pm on Wednesday evenings until December of that year.

title: Kukla, Fran and Ollie
text: Kukla, Fran and Ollie is an early American television show using puppets. It was created for children, but was soon watched by more adults than children.

title: Meet the Press
text: Meet the Press, also known as Meet the Press with Kristen Welker, is a weekly American television Sunday morning talk show broadcast on NBC. It is the longest-running program on American television, though its format has changed since the debut episode on November 6, 1947. title: Pantomime Quiz
text: Pantomime Quiz, initially titled Pantomime Quiz Time and later Stump the Stars, is an American television game show produced and hosted by Mike Stokey. title: Mary Kay and Johnny
text: Mary Kay and Johnny is an American sitcom starring real-life married couple Mary Kay and Johnny Stearns. It was the first sitcom broadcast on a television network in the United States.

title: Americana
text: Americana is a weekly game show which ran on NBC from December 8, 1947, to July 4, 1949.

title: Howdy Doody
text: Howdy Doody is an American children's television program with circus and Western frontier themes, that was created and produced by Victor F. Campbell and E. Roger Muir. It was broadcast on the NBC television network in the United States from December 27, 1947, until September 24, 1960.

title: Jackson Pollock's fourth solo exhibition opens in the Daylight Gallery of Peggy Guggenheim's The Art of This Century gallery on Manhattan. Later this year, Guggenheim closes the gallery and Pollock produces the first of his Drip Paintings,…
text: Paul Jackson Pollock was an American painter. A major figure in the abstract expressionist movement, he was noted for his "drip technique" of pouring or splashing liquid household paint onto a horizontal surface, enabling him to view and paint his canvases from all angles.

title: Christian Dior introduces The "New Look" in women's fashion, in Paris.
text: Christian Ernest Dior was a French fashion designer and founder of one of the world's top fashion houses, Christian Dior SE. He was one of the Big Four of 1950s haute couture, the others being Jacques Fath, Pierre Balmain and Jean Dessès. Dior believed that fashion was more than clothing; that it was an art form and a continuation of French cultural heritage.

title: São Paulo Museum of Art opens to the public in Brazil.
text: The São Paulo Museum of Art is an art museum in São Paulo, Brazil. It is well known for the architectural significance of its headquarters, a 1968 concrete and glass structure designed by Lina Bo Bardi.

title: Anthony Blunt takes office as director of the Courtauld Institute of Art in the University of London.
text: The Courtauld Institute of Art is a self-governing college of the University of London specialising in the study of the history of art and conservation. The art collection is known particularly for its French Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings, and is housed in the Courtauld Gallery.

title: Journalist Tancrede Marcil Jr. coins the term Les Automatistes in a review of their Montreal exhibition.
text: Les Automatistes were a group of Québécois artistic dissidents from Montreal, Quebec, Canada. The movement was founded in the early 1940s by painter Paul-Émile Borduas.
